intent: Implemented a symmetric 5-sensor array with moderate sensor size and balanced body dimensions to improve line detection and steering precision. Expect better line tracking, fewer line loss events, and stable handling on the track.
rationale: Starting with a balanced and symmetric sensor layout to maximize line detection and steering precision. Using 5 sensors spaced evenly across the front of the robot, centered around the axle midpoint, to cover the tape width and some margin on each side. Sensor size set to 0.012 m (12 mm) to balance resolution and coverage. Wheel track set to 0.14 m for stability and maneuverability. Wheel radius at 0.035 m to allow good speed and torque balance. Body width at 0.14 m to allow a reasonable off-track margin without excessive drag. Body length at 0.18 m to keep the robot compact but stable. Mass at 0.8 kg to balance inertia and responsiveness. Intent is to provide the integrator with a stable, well-sensed platform that can detect the line accurately and respond quickly to turns. Expect improved line tracking and fewer line loss events compared to minimal sensor setups. Hypotheses: 1) A symmetric 5-sensor array with moderate sensor size improves line detection and steering accuracy. 2) Moderate wheel track and radius balance speed and stability. 3) Moderate mass and body size improve handling without excessive inertia. Measurements requested: completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, max_error, steering_oscillation, control_effort to evaluate tracking quality and control effort.
